messages:
anya: FYI - after the midnight deploy some tenants hit 5xx spikes. looked into traces, seems tied to a rare mmap/munmap race when we try to promote contiguous small pages into a hugepage during offload promotion. repro sketch below.

mike: saw it too. +1 to the mmap race hypothesis. heapster logs show repeated WARNs then a segfault in promote_hugepage(). attaching minimal backtrace.

lee: quick note - this only happens when eviction + live compaction run concurrently with promotion path, right? iirc we do a slab coalesce that unmaps then remaps ranges.

anya: yes. pattern: eviction thread unmaps, promotion path expects a stable vma and races with munmap, sometimes both paths believe they own the remap which yields stale pointers.

sam: can you paste the logs?

anya: sure - snippet:
```
W 03:12:45.123 offload: mmap race detected addr=0x7f8a3c000000 len=2097152 tenant=blue
W 03:12:45.124 promote: attempted hugepage promote but vma changed -> abort
E 03:12:45.125 crash: null deref in promote_hugepage+0x4a
```

mike: stack: promote_hugepage -> coalesce_try_promote -> offload_write_path -> inference_execute. repeatable in ~1/50k requests in staging when we hammer with compaction load.

lee: naive fix would be a global mmap mutex during promote/coalesce, but that would blow tail latency. we need a rendezvous that's cheap in the common non-racing case.

sam: proposal: per-addr-chunk rendezvous tokens (64KB granularity). acquire is an atomic cmpxchg on a uint8 flag in a side table. if acquisition fails, caller takes fallback path (skip promotion). fastpath: single CAS, no syscall.

rachel: a fallback that skips promotion is fine as long as we observe the quality/latency impact. can we measure how often tokens collide under peak? if collisions are >0.1% we might need backoff.

mike: suggest experiment: instrument token collisions in staging with compaction on, run 10m requests, measure. I can add metrics: offload.rendezvous.attempts and .contended.

anya: pseudo-code for the idea:
```
bool try_promote(addr, len) {
  chunk = addr >> 16;
  if (!cas_acquire(token_table[chunk])) return false; // fallback
  if (!vma_stable(addr,len)) { release(token); return false; }
  do_promote();
  release(token);
  return true;
}
```

lee: looks okay. ensure token table is sharded to avoid cacheline thrash and allow NUMA-aware placement. also need eviction to respect token ownership when unmapping.

sam: good point - eviction should check token_table and if locked, either wait a bounded time or schedule unmap later. waiting in eviction might be ok with microseconds bound. let's avoid unbounded sleeps.

rachel: ops question: will this change require nightly migration? we prefer a staged rollout with feature flag off by default.

anya: yes. plan: add token table + metrics + feature flag. staging 100% for a week, canary 1% on prod for 24h. mike will own metric dashboards. sam will add guarded eviction logic.

mike: i'll land the metric patch and a small perf harness. tagging @qa for a frag/regression test. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy: rollout started for offload-rendezvous v1 -> canary 1%

anya: action items: anya - RFC doc + perf sims, mike - metrics + canary, sam - eviction wait path + bounded backoff, lee - ensure NUMA/shard placement notes. I'll create RFC in docs/rfcs tomorrow.

rachel: ack. thanks team. :thumbsup:
